headlines: US stock futures inch up as yields ease, inflation report looms
Inflation, Key Earnings Reports Cap Wall Street Pre-Bell; Asia Up, Europe Mixed
Mortgage rates jump for the sixth straight week, hitting both refinance and homebuyer demand hard
Refugees Set to Lose Health Coverage Under Trump Budget Law
Inside Man: How Chinese spies used lies, love and betrayal to target the Federal Reserve

cards.hearing: You may hear there's a big inflation report coming out today, the one that shows how fast everyday prices, like groceries and rent, are climbing.
cards.why: That report matters because it can shape how the Fed, which sets short-term interest rates, thinks about its next move, and that touches credit cards, car loans, and mortgages.
cards.but: But one report is a single data point. It is not a verdict on the whole economy, and it is not a signal to change a long-term plan.
cards.story: Picture checking the thermometer once and deciding the whole season is broken. One reading tells you about that morning, not about the year. A good plan is built for the whole year, not one number.
say: We watch these reports, but we do not rebuild your plan around one of them.
One data point is information, not a decision.

cards.hearing: You may hear that mortgage rates just climbed for the sixth week in a row, and that home buying and refinancing have both slowed down because of it.
cards.why: Higher rates mean bigger monthly payments on a home loan, so that touches a big household bill for anyone buying, selling, or refinancing a house.
cards.but: But rates move in cycles, and a plan built for decades does not need to react to six weeks of moves.
cards.story: Think of two neighbors. One waits by the window for the perfect rate before ever making a move, the other buys when it fits their life and adjusts later if rates shift. Over time, the second neighbor usually ends up further along.
say: We build your plan to handle rate swings, not to depend on guessing them.
This is a housing headline, not a reason to change your plan.

cards.hearing: You may hear stocks were a touch lower yesterday, and this morning things look calm, just easing up slightly before the bell.
cards.why: Small daily wiggles like this are just markets breathing, they are not a signal about your long-term plan.
cards.but: But a quiet, mixed morning like today is actually pretty normal, and normal is good.
cards.story: Picture a heartbeat on a monitor. If it never moved at all, that would be the scary part. The little ups and downs are just proof the system is alive and working.
say: Small moves like this are just noise, not news for your plan.
We expect wiggles like this, it's part of how markets work.
